author: j r
text_post: Assuming that you can get the dates you want and the hotel is not crap, this seems like a good deal.  Airfares right now are through the roof. I've seen some report on shady all-inclusive resort deals that are basically bait and switch situations.  The resort looks nothing like the pictures, half the facilities are closed, and your food options are so limited that you end up paying for food.  I'd say be careful before booking one of those. If it's just a regular hotel though, should be fine.  The one thing to look out for is whether they guarantee you a specific hotel or not.  If you know the hotel, you can look it up and see the location and find some reviews.  Sometimes, the deals say "at X Hotel or a comparable location."  Then you're rolling the dice.  They could get you in with a sweet hotel and then switch you to some crappy place 30 minutes outside of town.

author: Pokerbaby
text_post: I have bought a lot of shit off Groupon.  Never had any problem.  There is fine print, but it has always been the usual kind of stuff "offer expires Dec 31 XXX" and that kind of thing. Nothing "tricky".  The only travel experience I used with Groupon was booking Niagara falls hotels (easy drive from Toronto) so I am not sure about it for exotic destinations.  The site I use for travel is hotwire.com.  It has some amazing deals.  But I have come to learn that the better hotels seldom cut their rates too much under ANY circumstances.
